The upgrade window is part of durability — mixed-version machinery in @kolu/surface-daemon

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 28, 2026

Plan of record for issue #2028: extend the surface-daemon spine so the mixed-version window (new supervisor ⇄ old daemon over shared artifacts) is owned by the framework — typed convergence states, a framework drain protocol with policy-declared admission, versioned artifacts under a tolerant-reader law, and the #2027 test machinery shipped as a testlib. Second consumer: drishti's per-host agent becomes a durable daemon with a persistent metric ring.

Plan of record for #2028. Decided up front: extend @kolu/surface-daemon — no new package; drishti’s per-host agent is the second consumer, designed on paper before any framework code so the API is derived from two consumers; the capstone re-lands the parked gate-format change that caused the #2011 incident.

The window the framework created and then ignored

@kolu/surface-daemon sells durability: a daemon that survives its supervisor’s deploys. Durability creates the mixed-version window — a new-build supervisor talking to an old-build daemon through shared artifacts (pid gate, unix socket, state files) — and today the framework stops at detection primitives while every consumer discovers the window’s edges by hand. kolu found the cost in production: a gate-format change made the new reader refuse the legacy gate shape, so the recycle path had no pid to SIGTERM and Restart kaval silently did nothing.The #2011 incident: the parked branch’s pidGate.ts moved to a two-field pid\tstartUnixUs gate whose reader “accepts exactly this build’s two-field identity; it never interprets the retired one-field pid shape” — a legacy gate parsed as unsupported-format, gatePid() returned undefined, and Restart no-oped. No test could catch it: every test in the repo boots both daemon generations from one checkout. The full adoption is parked on branch osfacts-kolu-adoption (tip dc104661), kept reachable because drishti pins commits on that history.

The framework is further along than the issue’s framing suggests: since #1674, the supervisor already owns the convergence kit — identity types, policy, the pure decide() table, converge(), the endpoint machine.Specifically: ConvergenceIdentity (ordered contractVersion, match-only build), ConvergencePolicy&lt;Cap&gt;, BuildDrainFence, and the endpoint’s incompatible state plus gateless-squatter recovery. What kolu still hand-rolls, and what this plan graduates, is precisely bounded:

  1. The drain skeleton — arm the exit-observer before firing the drain RPC, race exit against a ceiling; ground truth is the process exiting, never the RPC resolving.drainAndAwaitExit at packages/server/src/padi/padiConvergence.ts:103, shared today by copy between the local endpoint arm and the remote ssh arm.
  2. Drain admission — the remote arm’s instance-keyed budget: a different daemon instance after our drain means another supervisor is fighting us → give up loudly; the same instance past the budget → adopt stale.admitDrain in remotePadiBinding.ts. The framework’s boolean BuildDrainFence is a degenerate case of this budget.
  3. The post-drain story as typed states — the remote arm’s anomaly union is app-typed, its cross-supervisor verdict lives in a sidecar flag with an ordering hazard, and the local arm can’t express adopt-stale at all.The union at packages/common/src/surface.ts:387; the crossSupervisorDetail sidecar has one set site, six clear sites, and a checked-first hazard in computeEntryFailedDetail (remotePadiBinding.ts:381). The local gap — decide() collapsing a fence-spent adopt to a bare adopt — is named in code at padiBinding.ts:738-741.
  4. The ssh arm itself — remotePadiBinding.ts bypasses converge() entirely and hand-spells the enactment switch over a raw decide(). Drishti’s daemon is remote-only, so this is the second consumer’s main path, not an edge case.
  5. The window tests — #2027’s fixture, watchdog, and previous-release e2e guard kolu’s window from packages/padi/src/upgradeWindow/, with machinery that is ~60–100% generic per file.

The API, derived from two consumers on paper

Setting kolu’s window and drishti’s window side by side is what fixes the API shape — each concern below names the framework piece, its home, and which consumer forced it.

Window concern Framework piece (new pieces in bold) kolu drishti
Who is running? frozen identity channel: controlCore fragment served by the daemon + probeDaemonIdentity dialed by the supervisorThe fragment’s key set is padi’s existing frozen wire, verbatim: stateRoot · surfaceVersion · controlCoreVersion · startedAt · commit · buildId, plus the drain verb — a parameterized envelope whose padi instantiation is byte-identical to today’s control.core.hello. The probe is supervisor-side machinery (a dialing client), so it lives in surface-daemon-supervisor — widening that package’s ALLOWED_EXTERNAL closure guard to admit @kolu/surface, a decision the guard’s own failure message invites; parking a dialing probe in the daemon package would put supervisor-only code in kaval’s staleKey hash root. It returns a bare ConvergenceIdentity plus the instance key; ConvergenceProbe assembly stays a consumer concern. padi’s hand-rolled control core migrates onto it; kaval keeps system.versionkaval’s identity rides a versioned procedure — a residual Pin-3 gap. Closing it means kaval adopting the control core: real daemon-surface work, explicitly a kaval-track follow-up, not silently absorbed. The parent note’s S1 milestone is superseded in shape by this row; surface-daemon.mdx is updated in this note’s landing PR. consumes it from day one
Is it my build? existing ConvergenceIdentity + decide() already wired new: readBakedIdentity("DRISHTI_AGENT")
How do I replace it? drainAndAwaitExit, run by the framework in both enactments — the drainable probe supplies only fire-the-verb and observe-exit plugs, so the skeleton has one home local + remote padi arms both migrate renewal over ssh rides it; the ssh exit-observer ships framework-sideIt hello-polls the fragment the framework itself owns, so every ssh consumer would otherwise rewrite the same plug.
When do I stop trying? drain admission as policy data: drainBudget: { maxAttempts, onGiveUp: "refuse" | "adopt-stale" } on the drainable policy — Cap-gated so a not-drainable policy cannot spell a budget; state owned inside the supervisor, one tracker per boot, surviving adoptsTwo semantics the sources disagree on, resolved here. (1) The budget survives adopts — remotePadiBinding.ts’s reset-on-adopt is not carried over, because each parent adopting its own spawn would wipe exactly the memory cross-supervisor detection needs, degenerating drishti’s two-parent topology into an alternating drain war. It remembers every (build, instance) lineage drained this boot; a drained lineage reappearing under a new instance ⇒ cross-supervisor give-up. (2) The boolean fence’s degenerate case (maxAttempts: 1) is padi’s local arm, not kaval — kaval’s not-drainable policy spells no budget at all, deleting today’s inert-fence ritual at ptyHost/index.ts:294 instead of renaming it. The instance key defaults to the fragment’s startedAt; no consumer-wired budget object exists. remote arm’s admitDrain deleted; kolu declares onGiveUp: "refuse" declares onGiveUp: "adopt-stale" — a losing parent keeps monitoring through a contract-compatible stale daemon instead of going dark
What state am I left in? ConvergenceAnomaly: adopted-stale | skew-refused | unconverged | cross-supervisor, each carrying detail plus its evidence. link-failed is deliberately not an armIt is a projection of the session’s connection state, produced by no convergence path, with a different clearing lifecycle — kolu already special-cases exactly this (remotePadiBinding.ts:756 clears only link-failed on a mere disconnect), and serveHostMap.ts:211 documents transport-vs-domain as separate axes. Each consumer unions it in at its own composition edge. The cross-supervisor arm, conversely, must be framework: the admission machinery is what detects it, and its absence is what forced kolu’s sidecar-flag hack. DaemonSession’s generic Conv parameter already accommodates the union; daemonSession.ts’s “convergence vocabulary lives in the app” prose gets updated in UW1. schema re-derives from it + unions link-failed app-side; the sidecar flag and its ordering hazard are deleted host-map entry carries it to the UI — “your other machine owns this host” is a typed state
One kit, both transports enactment-generic converge — endpoint-shaped and admit-shaped (convergeAdmit) enactments over one decide + drain skeleton + admission. The endpoint’s public boot-method trio goes internal: policy is fixed at construction; the public verbs are converge and recycleNo production caller invokes adoptOrEnsure/adoptOrSpawnOrRefuse outside converge, which already derives the bind method from policy; the public trio leaves the policy/method cross-pairing spellable. restart.ts and kolu’s restart steps keep the explicit recycle verb. UW1’s converge signature changes anyway; this rides the same break. (The bird’s-eye alternative — one mega “durable daemon object” — was hunted and refuted; no wholesale rewrite.) remotePadiBinding.ts’s hand-spelled switch deleted the only enactment drishti uses
Do both generations agree on the files? versioned shared-artifact discipline: registry + watchdog as testlib (UW2); versioned gate under a tolerant-reader law (UW4) registry array stays in kolu registers agent.pid, agent.sock, history.ring.json, logs
Can I test the window? ./upgrade-window.testlib subpath (UW2) upgradeWindow/ shrinks to registrations window tests arrive with the window code

What stays app policy, deliberately: the policy declarations, baked-identity env prefixes, drain ceilings/cadences as values, breadcrumb prose at the log edge, fatal-verdict classification, the link-state projection, and the nudge-human surface.

The API in one example

What a new consumer writes after UW1+UW2 — a fictional pulse daemon, both halves, complete except for its own surface cells. This is the note’s contract for what the phases must add up to:

// ── daemon side: runs inside the durable process ──────────────────────────
import {
  daemonMain, daemonProcessMain, readBakedIdentity, controlCoreFragment,
} from "@kolu/surface-daemon";

const ident = readBakedIdentity("PULSE"); // PULSE_BUILD_ID / PULSE_COMMIT_HASH, baked by nix
daemonProcessMain({
  name: "pulse-daemon",
  run: () => daemonMain({
    gatePath: join(stateDir, "pulse.pid"),
    socketPath: join(stateDir, "pulse.sock"),
    anchor: () => stateDir,
    lifetime: { kind: "idleTimeout", ms: 60 * 60_000, isIdle: () => liveConnections === 0 },
    router: implementSurface(pulseSurface, {
      // the frozen fragment: hello + drain, readable at ANY version skew
      ...controlCoreFragment({
        surfaceVersion: PULSE_CONTRACT_VERSION,
        buildId: ident.staleKey, commit: ident.navigableCommit,
        stateRoot: stateDir, startedAt: bootInstant,
        onDrain: persistStateThenStop,
      }),
      /* …pulse's own cells and procedures… */
    }),
    log,
  }),
});

// ── supervisor side: runs wherever the app supervises from ────────────────
import {
  createEndpoint, converge, survivableSpawnDriver, type ConvergencePolicy,
} from "@kolu/surface-daemon-supervisor";

const POLICY: ConvergencePolicy<"drainable"> = {
  capability: "drainable",
  onContractSkew: { kind: "drain-newer-else-refuse" },
  onBuildMismatch: { kind: "drain-and-replace" },
  drainBudget: { maxAttempts: 2, onGiveUp: "adopt-stale" }, // unspellable for "not-drainable"
};

const endpoint = createEndpoint({
  gatePath, socketPath,
  policy: POLICY,                              // fixed at construction — no boot-method trio
  baked: { contractVersion: PULSE_CONTRACT_VERSION, build: daemonBuild(myBakedId) },
  driver: survivableSpawnDriver({ binPath, args: ["--daemon"], env, unitPrefix: "pulse" }),
  connect: () => connectPulse(socketPath),     // the app's typed handshake — its soul
  log, onStatus,
});

const outcome = await converge(endpoint);      // probe → decide → drain/adopt/spawn, typed
if (outcome.anomaly) showOnEntry(outcome.anomaly);
// anomaly: adopted-stale | skew-refused | unconverged | cross-supervisor — never a silent no-op

A connector-shaped consumer (drishti’s ssh arm, kolu’s remote padi) swaps converge(endpoint) for convergeAdmit(...) with the same policy object; only the enactment differs.

Drishti — the durable per-host agent

Today drishti’s agent is the textbook ephemeral serveOverStdio consumer: every ssh dial provisions the parent-pinned nix build and spawns a fresh process, so agent state dies per reconnect and the parent’s 30-minute metric ring dies per deploy.Correcting the issue’s framing: history does not die with the tab — it lives in a per-host ring in the parent, replayed to any browser. What kills it is a parent restart (every home-manager deploy) and host removal; agent-side alert hysteresis and rate baselines die on every reconnect. Also today, skew is impossible by construction — spawn-per-dial means agent ≡ parent build. The durable daemon makes skew the steady state, which is exactly why drishti is the right second consumer: frequent deploys, two parent platforms, remote-only supervision, and a real cross-supervisor topology.

The design, with the author’s decisions baked in:

  • One flag-dispatched binary. --stdio becomes the front (frontDaemonOverStdio + reExecAsDetachedDaemon); --daemon runs the daemon serving the existing agent router over a unix socket. The parent’s wire is unchanged — the front relays bytes — so sshConnector, makeSession, and pumpRemoteSurface keep their shapes; the session upgrades to DaemonSession to expose convergence() and renew().
  • Everything under the state dir, deliberately. Gate, socket, and ring live in ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/drishti/, which is also the daemon’s anchor — not $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.On a default systemd host, closing the user’s last ssh session makes logind remove /run/user/$UID entirely — unlinking socket and gate while the detached daemon survives, leaving an invisible orphan no framework recovery can find and a successor racing it for the ring file. A state-dir socket persists across reboots as a stale file, which the pid gate and the endpoint’s socket-accepting probe already classify correctly. Lifetime: idleTimeout 60 minutes with zero live connections — twice the history retention, so any reconnect that could still see useful history finds the daemon alive, and abandoned hosts self-clean.
  • The ring moves into the daemon, and onto disk — with its window discipline stated. The ring and metricHistory stream move agent-side; the daemon persists history.ring.json (explicit v field) every 30 s and on drain, via the repo-canonical atomic write. A ring with an unknown v or unparseable content is preserved untouched and surfaced as a typed history-unavailable state — never a silently empty chart.The unknown-v case is the rollback window: an older successor reading a newer generation’s file — the #2011 shape (identifiable-but-refused) would otherwise reappear as a silent empty. Corrupt files are moved aside, never deleted. Both dispositions get covering tests: a planted v+1 ring and a truncated ring. History then survives reconnects, parent deploys, daemon renewals, and crashes — and drishti exercises all three artifact seams: gate, socket, state file. Alert hysteresis becomes durable as a side effect of living in the daemon.
  • Identity and convergence. The agent surface gains AGENT_SURFACE_VERSION = "1.0" and serves the controlCore fragment. Parent policy: drainable, drain-newer-else-refuse / drain-and-replace, drainBudget: { maxAttempts: 2, onGiveUp: "adopt-stale" } — all via convergeAdmit. Drishti-side convergence code is the policy declaration and the app-edge link-state projection; nothing else.The two-parent mixed-pin window, traced: one machine deployed, the other on yesterday’s pin. Builds don’t order (Pin 2), so there is no “right” winner. The surviving-adopts budget bounds the fight to maxAttempts drains per parent per boot; the first parent to observe a foreign respawn of a lineage it drained parks in cross-supervisor, and with onGiveUp: "adopt-stale" both parents keep monitoring through whichever build won — one wearing a typed anomaly naming the fight — until the pins converge. The alternating-drain scenario is pinned as a framework unit test in UW1, not left to topology luck.
  • Operational edges, named. The provisioning GC root must outlive the dial for the daemon’s lifetime; laptop-wake recheckAll must adopt, not respawn; drishti’s drv-stability CI node inverts from optimization to convergence signal.GC root: today’s root covers the ephemeral case; nix-collect-garbage deleting a running daemon’s closure is a UW3 bug to prevent. Wake: the front’s adopt path gives adopt-not-respawn for free, and the adopt e2e must include the field-realistic sequence — connect, close the last ssh session, reconnect, adopt with the ring intact. drv-stability: accidental agent-drv churn now means fleet-wide daemon renewals (history handoff makes this survivable, but the node stays required). Off-nix dev parents adopt whatever runs, per the existing off-nix decide row.

The testlib — window tests ship with the window code

#2027 built the machinery app-side; UW2 graduates the generic core into a new @kolu/surface-daemon export subpath ./upgrade-window.testlib.Following the kolu-io testlib-subpath precedent; .testlib.ts files are already excluded from every staleKey hash, so this adds zero identity churn. The subpath stays dependency-free: the fixture’s daemon-spawn guard becomes an injected hook (kolu wires @kolu/daemon-test-gate; drishti wires its own gate) rather than a package dependency drishti’s source-hydration setup could not resolve. Phases

Four PRs, strictly sequenced — each later phase consumes API the earlier one creates. Standing obligations: every phase updates the paired website/src/content/surface/ref-*.mdx reference pages in the same PR, and every phase posts an odu-impact verdict.odu consumes neither package at its current pin — odu serve (the parent note’s S2 tenant) is unshipped — so verdicts are expected none or adoption-opportunity for now; the obligation exists precisely so the ledger catches the moment that changes.

UW1 — the supervisor kit completes: drain, admission, anomaly, both transports

TL;DR: Framework: the convergence kit becomes whole — one converge/convergeAdmit pair over one decision table, drain and admission included, every skew outcome a typed state. Consumers: kolu’s three arms shed ~300 lines of hand-rolled convergence; policy moves to endpoint construction. Users: nothing visibly changes — except states that were silent (adopt-stale locally, cross-supervisor) now surface in the host UI.

What lands: drainAndAwaitExit (framework-run in both enactments), the policy-declared Cap-gated drain budget (surviving adopts, replacing BuildDrainFence), adopted-stale, the four-arm ConvergenceAnomaly, convergeAdmit, the boot-method trio going internal; kolu’s local and remote padi arms migrate in the same PR.

Done when: remotePadiBinding.ts no longer touches decide() directly nor defines its three hand-rolled converge functions, and the crossSupervisorDetail sidecar plus its checked-first hazard are deleted; kaval’s call site passes no budget and constructs no fence; the adoption-padi-upgrade VM arm still greps its breadcrumb green; a unit arm pins the previously-inexpressible local adopted-stale; the two-parent alternating-drain scenario is a framework unit test proving the fight terminates in cross-supervisor.Plus: daemonSession.ts’s convergence-vocabulary prose updated. No drishti pair yet (drishti consumes neither package); odu-impact verdict required.

Manual QA:

  • Boot the PR build over a production padi left by master (kolu normally, then relaunch from the PR checkout): the server log shows the padi build change on boot … draining the survivor once breadcrumb, terminals and kaval survive, scrollback intact.
  • Restart kaval from the UI (kaval chip → Restart) — the not-drainable recycle path, must behave exactly as today.
  • On a remote host at a different kolu build, open the host’s daemon dialog: the convergence state (adopt-stale/skew) shows as a named state, never a blank.

UW2 — identity fragment + the upgrade-window testlib

TL;DR: Framework: daemons gain one frozen way to say who they are (controlCore fragment + probeDaemonIdentity), and the mixed-version test machinery becomes an importable testlib. Consumers: padi’s hand-rolled control core is deleted; kolu’s upgradeWindow/ shrinks to registrations. Users: zero behavior change — padi’s wire is byte-identical.

What lands: the fragment (padi’s frozen key set, parameterized envelope), the probe (supervisor-side, ALLOWED_EXTERNAL widened, recorded), the ./upgrade-window.testlib subpath per the table above, supervisor.pid registered.

Done when: packages/padi/src/upgradeWindow/ contains no generic machinery; padi’s hello wire is byte-identical (existing dialPadiHello tests green, unchanged); the graduated matchers take the registry as a parameter and the watchdog enforces the tightened versionField discipline; ci::upgrade-window green on both platforms via the graduated harness.No drishti pair yet; odu-impact verdict required.

Manual QA:

  • Nothing should look different — this phase’s QA is confirming absence of change: boot kolu, restart padi and kaval from the UI, open the daemon info dialogs; all identical to master.
  • Skew smoke: kolu from master against the PR build’s surviving padi (and vice versa) — hello still answers, restart still works, both directions.
  • just ci (or the upgrade-window odu node) green on your machine — the graduated harness nix-builds the previous release tag and drives a real recycle.

UW3 — drishti adopts: the durable agent, paired era begins

TL;DR: Framework: first external consumer; .claude/rules/surface.md starts covering both daemon packages (paired drishti PR + odu verdict, permanently). Drishti users: metric history and alert state survive everything — reconnects, parent deploys, agent upgrades — and a host being supervised by your other machine shows as a named state instead of confusion.

What lands: kolu-side, the rules-file extension plus whatever small framework needs adoption surfaces; drishti-side, the durable agent per the design above (daemon+front, state-dir artifacts, on-disk ring with typed load dispositions, convergeAdmit policy with adopt-stale, registry + watchdog + window e2e, GC-root fix, wake-adopt).The bootstrap, stated: drishti has no daemon-capable previous release, so at landing the mixed-build arm runs against a synthetic previous — the same source built with a different baked buildId — driving a real build-axis drain over ssh; the real previous-tag resolver (with the identical-store hard refusal) arms itself at drishti’s first daemon-capable release tag.

Done when the proof paths are hit, not the features around them: (a) the reconnect-adopt arm — connect, close the last ssh session, reconnect — adopts the surviving daemon through frontDaemonOverStdio with the ring intact; (b) the synthetic mixed-build arm executes a build-axis drain-and-replace through the framework’s drainAndAwaitExit, and the successor serves history re-seeded from history.ring.json; (c) the planted v+1 and truncated-ring dispositions surface their typed states. Both PRs green, drishti pinned to final kolu HEAD.

Manual QA (on the drishti PR, against a real remote host):

  • Watch a host’s metrics for ~10 minutes, then restart the drishti parent (redeploy or kill + relaunch): on reconnect the chart still shows the full history — the headline feature.
  • ssh <host> ls ~/.local/state/drishti/ — agent.pid, agent.sock, history.ring.json present; close all your ssh sessions to the host, reconnect drishti: same daemon pid (adopted, not respawned), no history gap beyond the disconnect.
  • Suspend the laptop, wake: fleet recheck adopts (pids unchanged on the hosts).
  • Deploy a drishti with any agent-visible change: the host entry shows the drain/replace happening (no silent gap), and history survives the daemon swap.
  • If you have two machines: point both at one host at different drishti pins — both keep monitoring; one shows the cross-supervisor / adopt-stale state by name.
  • Corrupt test: ssh <host> 'echo garbage > ~/.local/state/drishti/history.ring.json', reconnect — a typed “history unavailable” state, never an empty chart; the file is moved aside, not deleted.

UW4 — capstone: the gate change that bricked, re-landed window-compatible

TL;DR: Framework: the pid gate becomes versioned identity (pid + start-instant, killing pid-reuse misidentification) under a tolerant-reader law — the first token of a gate file is the holder’s pid, in every generation; unknown trailing fields are ignored, never a refusal. Users: Restart works across every upgrade and rollback boundary — the #2011 brick becomes inexpressible. Kolu: unblocks OSF8.

What lands: the two-field writer (${pid}\t${startUnixUs}\n), the tolerant reader (a legacy gate reads as { pid, startUnixUs: undefined } — a valid, older gate whose holder can be signaled), acquirePidGate taking an injected readProcessIdentity (kolu and drishti supply osfacts-backed readers), identity comparison with a ±2 s tolerance on startUnixUs, and the booting-holder case named.Why not the parked branch’s design: dc104661’s reader refuses any shape but its own, which both re-expresses the #2011 brick against v1 gates and would brick again when a v2 reader meets a future v3 gate — the parked branch is the starting point for the writer and identity plumbing only. Why the tolerance: the wall-clock start instant is derived from /proc/stat’s btime at each read and shifts whole seconds under NTP steps, suspend, and VM pauses — strict equality would misjudge a live daemon as pid-reuse and re-create the brick from the other direction. The booting-holder case: a live-identity gate whose socket is not yet accepting is a holder in the gate-write→socket-listen window — waited on, not reaped. Scope: the gate-identity slice only; the rest of osfacts-kolu-adoption (memorySampler via osfacts, V2 facet UI) remains OSF8’s, which this phase unblocks — os-facts-tool.mdx’s OSF8 row gets a one-line pointer here.

Done when the incident is a red-turned-green test, in both directions: the graduated fixture plants a legacy one-field gate under a current supervisor and recycle succeeds by SIGTERM-ing the recorded pid (the exact #2011 failure); a unit pin feeds the two-field write through the literal legacy parse and extracts the pid (pid-first is the frozen rollback contract); a clock-perturbation test shifts startUnixUs within tolerance without losing the holder; the previous-release e2e crosses a version boundary where the previous binary still writes one-field gates; both platforms green; drishti pair green at final kolu HEAD.

Manual QA:

  • The incident, replayed: run master kolu (old one-field gate), quit the server (kaval survives), launch the PR build, hit Restart kaval — it must actually restart (gate pid found through the legacy shape). This exact sequence bricked in #2011.
  • The rollback: run the PR build (two-field gate), quit, relaunch master, Restart kaval — still works (old reader’s parseInt stops at the tab; pid-first is the contract).
  • Clock shake: on a test host, sudo date -s '+3 sec' (or suspend/resume) while a daemon runs, then Restart — the holder is still recognized (tolerance), not treated as pid-reuse.
  • Same two sequences on a drishti-monitored host for the agent daemon (the gate is shared API now).
